28mm to 1:35: Tabletop Infantry to Model Kit Scale

Taking a 28mm infantry figure and growing it to 1:35 model-kit scale is a big jump, and honestly it is a display move because a 1:35 human stands about 45.7mm to the eyes.

Back to all conversions1:35 to 28mm

The math

(45.7mm / 28.0mm) × 100 = 163.2%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level28.0mm Eye
  • Target eye level45.7mm Eye
  • Scale factor163.2%

Why you'd go big

A 28mm D&D figure grown to 163.2% becomes a ~1:35 human, which suits large dioramas or pairing with 1:35 kits. I do this when I want a spotlight hero in a model-kit-scale scene. The 63.2% enlargement smooths detail and gives a big paint surface.

Watch the proportions

28mm true-scale figures carry realistic proportions, so enlarging them reads correctly in a 1:35 context. Heroic figures enlarge into a chunky look — fine if the scene is heroic, odd if it is meant to be a realistic kit.

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini and measure with digital calipers before I post it.

I test every percentage on FDM before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Quick Answers

Is 28mm to 1:35 a display conversion?

Yes — it's a 163.2% upscale to model-kit scale, best used for a display hero or diorama rather than a playable figure.
